Interfaces

SurfaceProps

The DOM attributes of one entry as React props [S-DOM-1]: what surfaceAttributes returns, with aria-disabled and aria-readonly as booleans. Spreads onto button, input, div, or any element that receives the control's interaction.

SurfaceProvider()

function SurfaceProvider(props): FunctionComponentElement<ProviderProps<AutoSurfaceHandle | null>>;

Derive the surface from the page this tree renders. Put it near the root:

<SurfaceProvider config={surfaceConfig} flag={flags.agentSurface} webMcp expose>
  <App />
</SurfaceProvider>

useSurface()

function useSurface(
   entry, 
   deps, 
   target?
): void;

entry is the object register takes. deps are the values it was computed from; the entry is re-registered in place when they change, which is how availability and values stay current.

Transient states belong in deps too: a saving or loading flag, an open modal, anything the component uses to disable its own control. Left out, the surface keeps reporting the control available while the UI has frozen it, and an act runs into a disabled control ([S-REV-5]). For a state that spans the whole page, surface.freeze(reason) is the shorter route.

Functions need not be in deps: an act always runs the handler (and edit.set, more, requires.fulfill) of the latest render. The registration belongs to the pair of entry.id and target: when either changes, the previous pair is unregistered and the new one registered, and unmount unregisters the current pair. Strict Mode's extra mount and unmount leave the same table.

Parameters

entry

Entry

deps

DependencyList

target?

Surface = defaultSurface

Returns

void

useSurfaceProps()

function useSurfaceProps(
   entry, 
   deps, 
   target?
): SurfaceProps;

useSurface plus the control's attributes: registers entry while mounted (refreshing it in place when deps change) and returns the props the rendered control spreads, so the accessible name a browser agent or screen reader reads is the name observe() reports. The props follow the surface's live availability (surface.attributesFor): while the surface is frozen the control reads aria-disabled or aria-readonly with the freeze's reason, and the component re-renders when that changes.

const props = useSurfaceProps(entry, [available, reason]);
return <button {...props} disabled={!available} onClick={draft}>Draft</button>;
